acceptance_criteria: DirectSmtp wraps existing path unchanged. SES impl tested against LocalStack. Webhook impl rejects bad HMAC. MultiTransport runs both concurrently.
description:
## Why this issue exists

Receiving email on port 25 directly is operationally painful on all three major cloud providers. AWS, Azure, and GCP all restrict port 25 by default, and running a publicly exposed SMTP listener requires IP reputation management and abuse mitigation that cloud providers are better positioned to handle. Managed inbound email services (AWS SES inbound, Azure Communication Services) receive email on the operator's behalf, perform spam/abuse filtering, and deliver pre-vetted messages to a queue or storage bucket that stoa can consume.

This is symmetric with the outbound `OutboundMailer` trait: just as outbound mail has an abstraction over SMTP relay and HTTP API providers, inbound mail needs an abstraction over direct SMTP and managed cloud intake.

## Trait

```rust
#[async_trait]
pub trait InboundMailTransport: Send + Sync {
    /// Subscribe to incoming messages. Calls handler for each received message.
    /// Runs until cancelled. Implementations are responsible for acknowledging
    /// (deleting from queue) messages after successful handler invocation.
    async fn run(
        &self,
        handler: Arc<dyn InboundMailHandler>,
        cancel: CancellationToken,
    ) -> Result<(), InboundError>;
}

#[async_trait]
pub trait InboundMailHandler: Send + Sync {
    async fn deliver(&self, envelope: InboundEnvelope) -> Result<(), DeliveryError>;
}

pub struct InboundEnvelope {
    pub mail_from: String,
    pub rcpt_to: Vec<String>,
    pub message: Bytes,           // raw RFC 5322 bytes
    pub source: InboundSource,    // Direct | Ses | AzureAcs | Webhook
    pub received_at: DateTime<Utc>,
}
```

The existing direct SMTP server becomes `DirectSmtpTransport`, one impl of this trait. All inbound paths — direct SMTP, managed cloud, webhook — funnel into the same `InboundMailHandler`, which is the existing delivery pipeline (sieve, Delta Chat bridge, mailbox delivery, JMAP event push).

## Implementations

### DirectSmtpTransport (default, no feature flag)
The existing SMTP listener. Wraps the current server into the trait. Port 25/587/465. Used for on-premise, self-hosted, and any deployment where direct SMTP is acceptable.

### AwsSesInbound (feature: `aws-ses-inbound`)

Architecture: SES receipt rule → SNS topic → SQS queue → stoa polls SQS.

- At startup, optionally verify/create the SQS queue and SNS subscription (if `auto_provision = true` in config; otherwise assume pre-created by Terraform).
- Poll SQS `ReceiveMessage` in a loop (long-polling, 20s wait).
- For each SQS message: parse the SNS envelope, verify the SNS message signature (prevents spoofed deliveries — same concern as bounce webhook signature verification in stoa-egptk).
- Extract the S3 object key from the SES notification (SES stores the raw email in S3 per the receipt rule action).
- Fetch the raw email from S3.
- Call `handler.deliver()`.
- On success: delete the SQS message and optionally delete the S3 object.
- On handler failure: leave SQS message for retry (up to SQS visibility timeout); dead-letter queue for permanent failures.
- Uses ECS task role (no hardcoded credentials).

Config:
```toml
[inbound.ses]
queue_url = "https://sqs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/123456789/stoa-inbound"
s3_bucket = "stoa-inbound-mail"
region = "us-east-1"
auto_provision = false
```

### AzureAcsInbound (feature: `azure-acs-inbound`)

Architecture: Azure Communication Services email → Event Grid → Service Bus queue → stoa polls Service Bus.

- Poll Service Bus queue using the Azure SDK.
- Verify message authenticity via Service Bus shared access signature (or Managed Identity — prefer Managed Identity).
- Extract RFC 5322 payload from the ACS event envelope.
- Call `handler.deliver()`.
- On success: complete (delete) the Service Bus message.
- Uses Azure Managed Identity (no hardcoded credentials).

### WebhookInbound (feature: `webhook-inbound`)

Generic inbound for any provider that can POST email content to an HTTP endpoint (Mailgun inbound routing, SendGrid Inbound Parse, Postmark inbound, custom relays).

- Exposes `POST /intake/mail` on the JMAP HTTP port.
- Authenticates via HMAC-SHA256 shared secret (constant-time comparison — see crewcut pattern).
- Parses provider-specific envelope format (Mailgun multipart, SendGrid multipart, raw RFC 5322 POST).
- Calls `handler.deliver()`.
- Returns 200 on success, 4xx on auth failure, 5xx on delivery failure (provider will retry on 5xx).

Provider-specific parsers behind sub-feature-flags (`webhook-inbound-mailgun`, `webhook-inbound-sendgrid`, etc.).

### GcpPubSubInbound (feature: `gcp-pubsub-inbound`)

Architecture: external MX relay (e.g., a small Postfix on Cloud Run) → publishes to Pub/Sub topic → stoa subscribes.

GCP has no native managed inbound email equivalent to SES. The recommended pattern is a lightweight relay that accepts SMTP and publishes to Pub/Sub. stoa subscribes to the Pub/Sub subscription, extracts the RFC 5322 payload, and calls `handler.deliver()`.

Uses GCP Workload Identity.

## Multiple transports

A `MultiTransport` impl wraps N transports and runs them concurrently, each in its own task. This allows a deployment to accept both direct SMTP (for on-network peers) and managed inbound (for internet email) simultaneously.

```toml
[inbound]
transports = ["direct_smtp", "ses"]
```

## Acceptance criteria

- `DirectSmtpTransport` wraps existing SMTP server; all existing tests pass
- `AwsSesInbound` polls SQS, verifies SNS signature, fetches from S3, calls handler; tested against LocalStack
- `WebhookInbound` returns 403 on invalid HMAC, calls handler on valid payload; integration tested
- `MultiTransport` runs two transports concurrently; delivery from either reaches the mailbox
- All impls use workload identity (no credentials in config)
- Existing direct SMTP path unchanged when only `DirectSmtpTransport` is configured
design: Symmetric with OutboundMailer: same abstraction pattern, same feature flag approach, same workload identity requirement. WebhookInbound is the most portable option — works with any provider that supports HTTP callbacks, including custom on-premise relays.
